newsitem.title: USA: Nike says future orders up 54 percent.
newsitem.headline: Nike says future orders up 54 percent.

text.p: Nike Inc said Wednesday that orders for athletic footwear and apparel for delivery from December through April rose 54 percent over the year-earlier period to a record $4.1 billion.

Nike said in a statement accompanying its second-quarter earnings report that the rise was caused by growth in its core business and a continuing shift to such "futures" orders from "at once" business.
Nike also said that revenues from sales outside the United States in the quarter rose 93 percent over the year-earlier period.
And Nike said its U.S. apparel sales were up 93 percent on top of a 100 percent increase in the same quarter last year.
"It is rare that a company our size in any industry can generate the growth Nike has achieved over the past 24 months," Nike Chairman Philip Knight said in a statement.
"These record results are a testament to the strength of the Nike team, which has raised the measure of our brand strength to unprecedented levels throughout the world."
Knight also said U.S. sales of men's running shoes had risen 90 percent in the quarter and sales of men's basketball shoes were up 38 percent despite the relative maturity of the categories.
In Japan, revenues increased almost 200 percent on a constant dollar basis, he said.
Worldwide future orders were not materially affected by currency fluctuations Nike said.
The company reported order growth of more than 50 percent in key U.S. categories, including women's fitness, men's basketball, men's running and kids.

Consolidated gross margins for the quarter were 39.4 percent compared with 39.0 percent last year. Selling and administrative expenses were 25.2 percent of second quarter revenues, compared with 26.1 percent last year.
Nike had $267.5 million in cash and short-term investments as of November 30, up from $204.8 million a year earlier.
Nike said total international sales in the quarter were $779.2 million, up from $487.1 million a year earlier.
Total U.S. athletic goods revenue rose to $1.19 billion, up from $734.3 million a year earlier, including athletic apparel sales of $377.9 million, up from $195.8 million.
"Other brands," including casual shoes, fell to $133.6 million from $135.5 a year earlier.
